finite_full_hamiltonian.setup: On one fixed finite Q3 volume Lambda, identify the configuration Hilbert space with L2(R^d), d=8|Lambda|. Let H=P^2/(2chi)+V(Q), U_t=exp(-itH/hbar), and alpha_t(A)=U_t^* A U_t, where V is the exact real semibounded coercive Q3 polynomial and H is the self-adjoint closure of its Schwartz-core realization.
finite_full_hamiltonian.multiplier: For f in L_infinity(R^d), let M_f be multiplication by f and define D_ess(f)=diameter(essential range of f)=sup{|a-b|:a,b belong to the essential range of f}.
finite_full_hamiltonian.lower_bound: For every f in L_infinity(R^d), liminf as t tends to zero through nonzero values of ||alpha_t(M_f)-M_f|| is at least D_ess(f). Thus a nonessentially-constant bounded measurable configuration multiplier is not a point-norm C0 element of the exact finite-volume full-Hamiltonian action.
finite_full_hamiltonian.real_exact_limit: If f is real, D_ess(f)=ess sup f-ess inf f. Scalar midpoint subtraction gives ||alpha_t(M_f)-M_f||<=D_ess(f) for every t, so the two-sided nonzero-time limit exists and equals D_ess(f).
finite_full_hamiltonian.scope: The theorem is finite-volume and concerns multiplication operators in the canonical Schrodinger representation. It neither classifies every continuous element of the full action nor excludes compact, temporally smeared, resolvent-smoothed, dressed, strict-topology, strong-star or state-weighted carriers.

lebesgue_packet_proof.essential_range_selection: Given a,b in the essential range and eta>0, the level sets {|f-a|<eta} and {|f-b|<eta} have positive measure. Choose Lebesgue points x,y of precise representatives in those sets and a normalized compactly supported smooth approximate-identity packet phi_(x,epsilon).
lebesgue_packet_proof.boost: For t nonzero put p_t=chi(y-x)/t and psi_(t,epsilon)=exp(i p_t.Q/hbar)phi_(x,epsilon). The boost commutes with M_f, so its time-zero expectation is the packet average at x.
lebesgue_packet_proof.free_density_transport: For the free group U_t^0, the exact Galilean identity yields |U_t^0 psi_(t,epsilon)(q)|^2=|U_t^0 phi_(x,epsilon)(q-(y-x))|^2. Only the modulus is used; the boosted vector itself need not converge because of its divergent phase.
lebesgue_packet_proof.two_sided_compact_segment: For s between zero and t, s/t belongs to [0,1] for both signs of t. The translated packet centers lie on the fixed compact segment x+(s/t)(y-x).
lebesgue_packet_proof.polynomial_duhamel: If deg V=m, polynomial translation gives |V(q+a)|<=C_(x,y,V)(1+|q|^m) uniformly for a on that compact segment. Free evolution preserves Schwartz space with locally bounded seminorms. At every fixed epsilon this yields sup_s ||V U_s^0 psi_(t,epsilon)||<=C_epsilon and ||(U_t-U_t^0)psi_(t,epsilon)||<=C_epsilon |t|/hbar.
lebesgue_packet_proof.expectation_and_limits: The operator norm dominates the absolute moving-vector expectation. First take the two-sided limit t->0 at fixed x,y,epsilon; then use the approximate identity at the Lebesgue points and finally let eta->0. Taking the supremum over essential-range a,b proves the lower bound.
lebesgue_packet_proof.quantifier_order: The safe order is eta, then the two Lebesgue points, then fixed epsilon, then two-sided t->0, then epsilon->0, then eta->0. No epsilon-uniform Duhamel constant is asserted or required.

joint_standard_cylinder.embedding: For finite Lambda containing a nearest-neighbor bond {x,y}, let j_x(A)=A tensor I_(Lambda minus {x}). Let beta^(xy) be the isolated nonzero bilinear bond flow and alpha^Lambda the exact full-Q3 finite-volume flow.
joint_standard_cylinder.prior_bond_classification: R-167 v3.0 proves that the beta^(xy) point-norm continuous standard cylinders j_x(A) are exactly j_x(M_f) with f in L_infinity(R^8).
joint_standard_cylinder.scalar_intersection: The new full-Hamiltonian theorem applied to the lifted multiplier f(q_x) makes alpha^Lambda point-norm continuity equivalent to f being essentially constant. Therefore C(beta^(xy)) intersect C(alpha^Lambda) intersect j_x(B(L2(R^8))) equals the scalar multiples of I_Lambda.
joint_standard_cylinder.boundary: This is a simultaneous-continuity classification only inside the canonical standard one-site cylinder. It is not a classification of either full continuous-element algebra and is not a no-go for unsplit common dynamics, dressed embeddings, multi-site compacts, temporal smears, resolvent carriers, local-strict carriers or weaker topologies.

surviving_positive_route.statement: A viable spatial common-alpha route must avoid requiring a nontrivial canonical one-site cylinder to be simultaneously point-norm continuous for every isolated bond subflow and the full Hamiltonian. The v3.0 background-uniform summable single-toggle shell theorem remains the exact sufficient target.
surviving_positive_route.missing_model_lemma: For an interaction-adapted or dressed core, prove compatible embeddings and a background-uniform bounded bond-form commutator estimate whose distance profile has summable Z3 shells. Duhamel differentiation would then produce the v3.0 single-toggle weights. No such exact-Q3 estimate or noncollapsing dressed core is proved here.
surviving_positive_route.literature_firewall: The audited oscillator and resolvent-algebra dynamics theorems use bounded intersite interactions, subquadratic or Fourier-regular forces, or other hypotheses not met simultaneously by the exact quartic onsite plus unbounded bilinear Q3 coupling. They are not imported as exact-Q3 common-alpha theorems.
